rules: Regular election for a full six-year term (2027-2033). Plurality winner; no runoff; ranked-choice voting is not used for this race. Four candidates on the ballot: Peggy Flanagan (DFL), Michele Tafoya (R), Marisa Simonetti (independent), Rebecca Whiting (Libertarian). Registered write-in candidates (Secretary of State list): Oriana Peral Lorainne Baker, Alycia R. Gruenhagen, Jay Willms (https://www.sos.mn.gov/media/cx5fynrb/registered-write-in-requests-2026.pdf). Absentee voting began September 18, 2026; in-person early voting with direct tabulation began 18 days before the election. Absentee and mail ballots must be received by Election Day to count. Minnesota has no party registration. Polls close at 8 p.m. Central; results are usually reported on election night. Sources: https://www.sos.mn.gov/about-the-office/news-room/voting-in-the-november-3-general-election-begins-september-18/ ; https://www.kaxe.org/elections/2026-10-19/early-voting-opens-in-mn-midterms-as-absentee-ballots-roll-in

candidates.name: Peggy Flanagan
candidates.bio_short: Flanagan has been lieutenant governor since 2019 and served in the Minnesota House from 2015 to 2019. She is a citizen of the White Earth Nation and began her career as a community organizer; she won the DFL Party endorsement on May 30, 2026.
candidates.primary_result: Won the August 11, 2026 DFL primary with 59.0% (411,853 votes) over U.S. Rep. Angie Craig (39.4%) and four others.

candidates.name: Michele Tafoya
candidates.current_or_last_office: Former sports broadcaster (has not held public office)
candidates.bio_short: Tafoya is a former sports journalist who worked for CBS, ABC/ESPN and NBC, including as NBC Sunday Night Football's sideline reporter from 2011 to 2022. After leaving broadcasting she became a political commentator. President Trump endorsed her on October 12, 2026.
candidates.primary_result: Won the August 11, 2026 Republican primary with 52.1% (211,813 votes) over Adam Schwarze (24.0%), Royce White (11.2%) and six others.

candidates.name: Marisa Simonetti
candidates.bio_short: Simonetti is a business owner running as an independent, according to the Wikipedia candidate list (citing EP Local News, March 2025). No FEC financial summary was found for her.

candidates.name: Rebecca Whiting
candidates.current_or_last_office: Farmer; Libertarian nominee for U.S. Senate in 2024
candidates.bio_short: Whiting is a farmer who was the Libertarian nominee for U.S. Senate in Minnesota in 2024, per Wikipedia. Her FEC committee reported $3,756 raised through October 14, 2026.
candidates.primary_result: Libertarian Party nominee (no contested primary result listed).

events.what: Sen. Tina Smith announced she would not seek reelection.

After a fatal shooting by an ICE agent in Minneapolis, immigration enforcement became a central issue in the DFL primary; Flanagan called for overhauling and later replacing ICE, while Craig defended her votes, coverage cited by Wikipedia reported.
Sen. Tina Smith endorsed Flanagan in the DFL primary, Politico reported.
Rep. Angie Craig withdrew from the DFL endorsement process and went straight to the primary.
Flanagan won the DFL Party endorsement by acclamation at the state convention.
Primaries: Flanagan won the DFL primary with 59.0% over Craig; Tafoya won the Republican primary with 52.1%.
Absentee voting for the November 3 election began.
Former President Barack Obama endorsed Flanagan, KSTP reported (exact date not verified; cited by Wikipedia on Oct. 26).
President Trump endorsed Tafoya at a rally and on Truth Social; Tafoya said she would work with him when he is right and stand up to him when he is wrong, MPR News reported.
Flanagan and Tafoya met in the race's only scheduled debate, hosted by MPR News in St. Paul.

early_vote.summary: Minnesota Secretary of State: 202,252 absentee ballots accepted by mail or in person in the first four weeks of absentee voting (which began Sept. 18), as relayed by KAXE; the office's Oct. 2 release reported 63,396 accepted as of Oct. 1 (26,174 in person, 37,222 by mail). Minnesota has no party registration, so there is no partisan breakdown.

notes_uncertain: Newer Secretary of State absentee updates after Oct. 16 were not retrieved (the site blocked automated access); the 202,252 figure is the SoS number as reported by KAXE (https://www.kaxe.org/elections/2026-10-19/early-voting-opens-in-mn-midterms-as-absentee-ballots-roll-in).

Wikipedia poll footnotes label Simonetti and Whiting inconsistently (e.g., 'Simonetti (L) & Whiting (G)'); on the ballot Simonetti is independent and Whiting is Libertarian. Footnotes are copied as written.
Mail-ballot receipt deadline (Election Day) is from standard Minnesota law and county notices; not re-verified on the state site for 2026.
The 'January 2026' ICE-shooting item is dated from an archived Star Tribune link (archived 2026-01-14); exact date not verified.
Marisa Simonetti: little independent biographical information found; no FEC financial summary.
Ages are as of Election Day (2026-11-03), computed from birth dates on the candidates' Wikipedia pages.
